title: Framework–PBC coefficient equivalence before smooth purity transport
statement:
Fix the finite-field datum $(p,a,q,k_0,k)$ of [def-weil-finite-field-fiber], a prime $\ell\ne p$, and an algebraic closure $\Omega/\mathbf Q_\ell$. Let $W$ be a separated finite-type $k$-scheme [def-weil-scheme-morphism-properties]. For each finite intermediate field $E$ of $\Omega/\mathbf Q_\ell$, let $\mathcal C^s_E(W)$ be the raw rationalization [def-weil-rationalization-karoubi] and $\mathcal C^p_E(W)$ the raw rationalization [def-weil-pbc-rational-category]. Write $S_{F/E,W}$ for strict-tower scalar extension in the former and $T_{F/E,W}$ for ordinary completed-ring scalar extension followed by rationalization in the latter [prop-weil-pbc-scalar-extension].

There are canonical exact $E$-linear equivalences $J_{W,E}:\mathcal C^s_E(W)\simeq\mathcal C^p_E(W)$. After the quotient-normalized completed-coefficient presentation identification [def-pur-completed-coefficient-presentation-transport], they are induced by the identity of the common full integral subcategory of [lem-weil-pbc-integral-stratified-perfect-characterization], and send an integral object to itself and $u\otimes e$ to $u\otimes e$. Their inverses have the same formulas in that common presentation. Their shift comparisons are induced by the identity of ambient complexes.

The specified completion maps $\chi_{F/E}$ of [lem-weil-finite-free-completed-scalar-comparison], together with the ordinary balanced coefficient-presentation comparisons, give exact natural isomorphisms
$$j_{W,F/E}:J_{W,F}S_{F/E,W}\xrightarrow{\sim}T_{F/E,W}J_{W,E},\qquad j=Q_F(\chi^{-1})$$
in the common intrinsic presentation. Here $Q_F$ denotes raw scalar localization. With $a^s$ the specified framework associator [lem-weil-scalar-extension-composition], normalized by the quotient-cocone equation of [lem-fix-scalar-completion-associator], and $a^p$ the tensor associator [prop-weil-pbc-scalar-extension], these maps satisfy
$$a^p_{M,F,E}\circ T_{M/F,W}(j_{W,F/E})\circ j_{W,M/F,S_{F/E,W}K}=j_{W,M/E}\circ J_{W,M}(a^s_{M,F,E}).$$
They respect the specified shift comparisons, the four-field pentagon and the unit comparisons. In particular $S_{E/E,W}$ is identified with the identity by the rationalized inverse completeness map, rather than taken literally to equal the identity; its transport through $J_{W,E}$ is $j_{W,E/E}$, since $T_{E/E,W}=1$.

On $\mathcal C_W$ of [def-weil-algebraically-closed-coefficients] and $\mathcal P_W$ of [def-weil-pbc-qbar-category] there is a canonical exact $\Omega$-linear equivalence
$$J_W:\mathcal C_W\xrightarrow{\sim}\mathcal P_W.$$
Its object formula is $J_W(E,K)=(E,J_{W,E}K)$. If $u:S_{M/E,W}K\to S_{M/F,W}L$ represents a morphism, its arrow formula is
$$J_W[M,u]=[M,j_{W,M/F,L}\circ J_{W,M}(u)\circ j_{W,M/E,K}^{-1}].$$
At each common field this is a bijection of Hom groups, commuting with further scalar transport; it and its inverse induce inverse maps on the Hom colimits. The equivalence and its inverse preserve finite-stage inclusions up to their specified unit comparisons, shifts and the common-stage distinguished triangles [def-weil-pbc-common-stage-cones]. No Karoubi completion is taken.

proof.text: The finite-type morphism to Spec k makes W locally Noetherian and compact, hence Noetherian. Apply exists_topologicalKrullDim_le. The cardinality of k0 identifies its characteristic with p, hence so does k; the prime ell distinct from p is nonzero in k. Map this field unit through GammaSpecIso, the structure morphism, and the germ to every stalk. This works also for empty W.

proof.text: The stage morphism inclusion isomorphism has identity components after the pair-functor equality. Transport the finite rational equivalence through the equality of its source coefficient type, field, algebra and cached category; abstract equality elimination avoids expanding field operations. Compose the included finite counit with the forward inclusion comparison, then cancel the fully faithful pair functor to obtain the inverse inclusion isomorphism. The defining cancellation equation is exactly the required pair counit equation. The forward comparison components are equality transports, so their composite with the included finite counit is heterogeneously that counit.
